original.target_description: Study 1, first condition, education comparison among Trump voters: college degree versus lower education, incorrect crowd-size choice, p. 140 Results/Figure 3 panel A. The p. 6 locator identifies the voter comparison rather than the strong-approval comparison on PDF p. 7.

n.quote:

n.sample_role: Analytic respondent count for the college-versus-lower-education comparison among Trump voters is not explicitly reported.
n.exclusions: Third-party voters excluded generally; education-specific missingness/exclusions and final subgroup counts not given.

es.quote:
While only 11 percent of less educated Trump supporters chose the wrong
                image as having more people, 26 percent of Trump supporters with college
                degrees selected the incorrect photo (difference of proportions p = .054).

notes: Printed descriptive candidates: 11 percent incorrect among less educated Trump supporters and 26 percent among college-educated Trump supporters, with difference-of-proportions p = .054. Neither an odds ratio nor a numerical comparative effect/test statistic is printed. No OR was derived. Figure 2 gives 218 Trump voters in the first condition, a candidate parent sample only: it does not explicitly establish the final education-comparison denominator or education missingness. Figure 3 caption gives education definitions but no subgroup counts; therefore analytic N remains null. Separate strong-approver education comparison on p. 141 reports p = .025 and Figure 3 shows 10% and 28%; it must not be merged with the voter comparison. The stated PDF p. 6 locator resolves this row to the voter comparison. Only assigned unfinished original fields were examined for output; other fields and replication/success are unassigned placeholders.
